To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new method to characterize the molecular weight distribution of a DNA or RNA sample based on the intensity profile of the sample’s electrophoretic line profile.
we developed a tool for the analysis of gel electrophoresed samples that is easy to use and provides information that is difficult to obtain by any other means.
a software tool for deconvolving nucleic-acid size distributions from gel electrophoreses has been developed and applied for quality control of DNA-sequencing libraries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the characterization of DNA-fragment size distributions, and we present the first application of the method to the analysis of NGS libraries.

the development of a software tool to analyze gel-electrophoretogram profiles, and we demonstrate its application in the deconvolution of nucleotide length distributions in DNA libraries prepared by the Illumina TruSeq DNA LT protocol.
the development of gel-electrophoresis analysis tools for NGS library preparation and characterization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this software tool is an important and useful addition to the repertoire of tools for DNA-sample characterization.
the software tool described here can be used to characterize DNA samples, including NGS libraries.

this is an interesting and useful method, which can be used for quality control of NGS libraries, but it does not replace the current standard, the Bioanalyzer® system, and is not suitable for routine use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have created a tool that is able to deconvolute the length distribution of a DNA sample based on a single lane of gel electrophoretic data.
we have developed a software tool to analyze the length distribution of DNA fragments from a gel-electrophoretogram.

this tool can be used to characterize the size distributions of DNA molecules in a sample, and it is especially helpful when the sample contains multiple bands of molecules that are not resolved by gel electrophoreses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gel electrophoreses can be a useful tool for NGS library QC, even though the method is not as widely used as automated gel imaging systems.

the deconvolution tool is a useful, low-cost alternative to existing automated systems for DNA-fragment size distribution analysis and that, in some cases, the deconvolution approach may be more informative than automated methods.

the method can provide useful information on library quality control, including the average size of DNA fragments, the presence of DNA fragments of a specific size (e.g. adapters, primers, or fragments of interest), and the degree of sample degradation.
